capabilityIntro: Skarion Stormwater prepares drainage GIS inventories and traceable handoff files from records supplied by the prime. Start with one basin, one inspection export or a bounded culvert backlog and agree on what the owner's reviewer can accept.
buyerRoles: Drainage project managers reconciling as-builts before a prime-led owner handoff
GIS leads preparing owner-schema asset layers and records for import
Inspection operations managers linking reports, photos and CCTV indexes to asset IDs
Public works asset staff working with an assigned civil or GIS reviewer

capabilities.title: Drainage asset GIS production
capabilities.summary: Build owner-schema points and lines for inlets, manholes, outfalls and pipes with stable IDs and source references.
inputs: As-built plans, owner GIS features or prime-approved field tables
Destination schema, coordinate reference system and agreed map extent
Owner ID rules and approach to unknown fields
outputs: Editable asset layers in the agreed format
Asset-to-source crosswalk and map for reviewer orientation
Geometry, connectivity and missing-attribute exception register
checks: Validate unique IDs and required fields for each feature type
Check pipe endpoints resolve to the expected asset or an explicit exception
Reconcile input scope against staged, queued and accepted feature counts

capabilities.title: Inspection records reconciliation
capabilities.summary: Prepare a relationship table between the owner asset register and the inspection records supplied by the prime.
inputs: Owner asset export with original IDs and permitted legacy aliases
Inspection report, CCTV or photo index with observation and source fields
Owner rules for duplicates, attachment references and condition codes
outputs: Asset-to-inspection crosswalk with match method and review status
Batch manifest recording input counts and source file versions
checks: Confirm source record IDs remain visible for every proposed link
Prevent duplicate evidence from being exported as a second accepted relationship
Retain original observations and request a reviewer decision on contradictions

capabilities.title: Culvert and structure registers
capabilities.summary: Consolidate prime-supplied culvert records into an editable, source-based register with a short field follow-up list.
inputs: Owner asset IDs, road references and inventory boundaries
Recorded dimensions and materials with their source and measurement units
Prime photo indexes and approved condition vocabulary
outputs: Asset register with source documents and attachment keys
Review queue for unseen outlets, conflicting locations and missing records
Schema dictionary specifying units, unknown values and status meanings
checks: Preserve a missing dimension or unobserved outlet explicitly
Verify each photo key links to the owner-authorized file manifest
Compare the recorded road or station with the original source before release

capabilities.title: Reviewer-ready closeout packaging
capabilities.summary: Organize the GIS delivery, exception queue and source manifest into a documented draft release for the prime or asset owner.
inputs: Prime-approved release extent, naming conventions and file formats
Delivery system import rules and person authorized to accept the batch
Approved way to exchange network drawings, images and field evidence
outputs: Release manifest with filenames, record counts and revision status
Owner review copy and open decisions grouped by responsible role
Pilot acceptance summary and next-batch scope notes
checks: Reopen the exported layers and validate rows against the manifest
Confirm queued items remain distinguishable from accepted data
Review that attachments, attribution and data-transfer rules match the agreed scope

formats: Editable GIS layer and agreed attribute schema
CSV crosswalk, source manifest and exception list
Map PDF or review image and draft release notes
requirements: Agree on the review boundary, record count and expected geometry accuracy before production
Supply the target coordinate system, units, IDs and destination schema
Assign a prime reviewer and an approved transfer route for source files
boundaries: Field verification and surveyed locations remain with the prime or qualified field partner
The assigned engineer owns hydrologic or hydraulic modeling, permit determinations and professional approvals
Owner reviewers control production release and any change to approved condition or asset values

projects.title: Basin 07 drainage inventory
projects.summary: Trace a fictional storm network to plan and inspection records while keeping one downstream connection open for review.
projects.imageAlt: Synthetic basin and storm pipes with mapped connections in teal and a connection awaiting review in dashed amber.
projects.context: In this fictional scenario a prime needs to reconcile mixed as-built sheets and inspection evidence before assembling an owner handoff. The downloadable extract holds four point features and two pipes. The graphic illustrates the broader inventory workflow and is schematic. The sample coordinates are fictional WGS 84 values.
constraints: Preserve source keys and the owner's published feature IDs in the draft
An upstream pipe endpoint is known while the downstream terminus of P-209 has no confirmed asset ID
Use the editable extract for workflow review. The exhibit is a schematic and has no surveyed position

approach.title: Catalog drainage evidence
approach.text: Index fictional plans D-01 to D-04 and CCTV 017 using stable source keys. Associate each point and pipe with its most relevant single record for this small extract.

approach.title: Link geometry and asset IDs
approach.text: Use coordinate pairs consistent with RFC 7946 and keep a shared asset ID across the geometry file and source crosswalk. Compare known pipe endpoints against the related point coordinates.

approach.title: Keep the unknown endpoint open
approach.text: Retain the plan-derived geometry for P-209 as a draft. Leave its downstream ID empty and record the action that the civil or GIS reviewer must take before release.

deliverables: Six-feature GeoJSON extract with source keys and pipe-endpoint fields
Six-row asset-to-source crosswalk with release state
Open connection ticket for P-209 with reviewer role and acceptance evidence
verification: Four point features and two lines are present with unique asset IDs
The crosswalk maps one row to each feature and agrees on its source key and state
P-107 resolves to both known assets. P-209 resolves to MH-208 upstream and retains a null downstream ID
The issue register connects EX-01 to P-209 and its fictional plan record
projects.review: GIS lead verifies geometry, IDs and field mapping. The prime's drainage reviewer resolves the P-209 downstream link, then separately approves owner import.

files.description: Six synthetic features with coordinates, source keys and draft pipe connections.

files.description: Six asset IDs with fictional evidence records and match or exception state.

projects.title: CCTV inspection record reconciliation
projects.summary: Compare exact links, potential aliases and unresolved inspection records before sending relationships to an owner system.
projects.imageAlt: A fictional inspection relationship queue showing a matched record, an alias for review and an unmatched record.
projects.context: A synthetic drain inspection index has seven incoming rows. Three rows use exact owner IDs. Four need a different disposition because of an alias, missing registry match, conflicting condition and duplicate inspection. These files demonstrate relationships between the source report, registered asset and human review state.
constraints: Retain the original asset ID and raw condition text from each input row
Potential aliases and condition conflicts stay in review until the owner signs off
Attachment keys in the sample are fictional placeholders without included media

approach.title: Establish the asset registry
approach.text: Use a four-asset synthetic master table that includes one reported legacy alias. Use canonical IDs for all staged exact relationships.

approach.title: Separate record dispositions
approach.text: Apply exact owner-ID matching first. Then route alias candidates, unknown asset IDs, conflicts and duplicate evidence to explicit review states. Preserve the source key and candidate identity.

approach.title: Guard the release file
approach.text: Stage exact links as candidates for owner review. Keep the raw condition and the registry condition in separate fields so a reviewer can inspect disagreement without altering either source.

deliverables: Four-row synthetic asset registry with rule inputs
Seven-row inspection relationship and QA queue
Disposition and owner action visible on each intake row
verification: Every canonical or candidate asset ID appears in the registry
Three rows are exact links and four have distinct review states
CCTV-23 preserves Poor from the source while the related registry records Fair
CCTV-26 references CCTV-11 as duplicate evidence and remains excluded from the matched subset
projects.review: The inspection delivery lead verifies source-report keys, attachment availability and duplicate evidence. The assigned owner reviewer confirms proposed aliases and resolves condition conflicts before import.

files.label: Synthetic owner asset registry (CSV)
files.description: Four fictional asset IDs, a legacy alias and recorded conditions.

files.label: Inspection record QA queue (CSV)
files.description: Seven inspection records with original values, match disposition and reviewer action.

projects.title: Rural culvert register and field follow-up
projects.summary: Organize culvert dimensions, road references and photo keys into a small register with clear field follow-up.
projects.imageAlt: A diagrammatic culvert section with an observed inlet, recorded span and downstream outlet pending field confirmation.
projects.context: This fictional register represents a six-record extract from a rural culvert backlog. The hypothetical prime provides road-log and inspection data. Three rows are ready for owner review and three need either field confirmation, documented evidence or a road-log cross-check.
constraints: Span and rise are recorded in millimeters and kept blank when the source is missing
Photo references are illustrative keys. No real photographs or georeferenced locations are included
Field survey, hydraulic adequacy and repair prioritization remain with the prime and engineer

approach.title: Normalize source records
approach.text: Align controlled material terms and keep recorded dimensions, stations, source keys and photo identifiers available for every populated field.

approach.title: Disclose incomplete evidence
approach.text: Flag the inaccessible outlet, mismatched road reference and missing measurement as distinct issue types. Do not copy a nearby culvert's dimensions or transfer a condition grade.

approach.title: Assign the next review
approach.text: Have the field lead resolve an unobserved outlet, the GIS reviewer reconcile the road reference and the inspection lead obtain the missing dimension evidence.

deliverables: Six-row editable culvert register including original record keys and photo references
Field follow-up queue grouped by the responsible reviewer
Inspection status separated from designed capacity or repair recommendation
verification: Asset IDs in the follow-up queue exist in the register and are unique
Three rows are ready for review and three have assigned follow-ups
CV-32 has an unknown outlet and no outlet photo key. CV-34 keeps blank measurements
The source road and target road remain separate on the mismatched CV-33 item
projects.review: The culvert inventory lead verifies units and attachment references. Assigned field and GIS reviewers resolve open items before the responsible reviewer clears any actual asset record.
